Problem statement: CFRFARM-37951 FRU ISO Requote Drastically Increased Premium
Description:
There was a recent requote of a new business FRU ISO policy where the premium went from $587 to over $6,000 (INC5190886).  It looked like the PL Property and PL Auto were very high, and the Base Rate Personal factor was a 1.0 when we expected a much smaller factor
Product: ISO Farm Umbrella - Phase 2 new business

From Prod Support resolution notes on INC5225823:

Our analysis shows that in the older ratebook (FRU Ratebook SD version 2020.05.01.26.0.0.01), the "FRU Base Rate Factor Personal" rate table was present, and getRateFactorAsBigDecimalNS(ratinginfo, FRUMBRELLA, BaseRatePersonal) was pulling the correct factor.

As a result, getRateFactorAsBigDecimalNS(ratinginfo, FRUMBRELLA, BaseRatePersonal) defaults to a factor of 1.00.

A few things contributed to this issue. We had a GSLB issue, when we moved to Dallas. We've done some work to get Dallas spun up and functioning with the GSLB configuration. That was working, but we found that there was a leftover config within the delegation zone that has GSLB still configured. Anything in Dallas we'll have issues with since this configuration is still in there. We have a Change going in to remove that configuration. It's DNS resolution from a global LB perspective will also get responses from the other two entries within the delegation zone consistently.
gslb.amfam.com has following name servers:
nhqnsglb1
grlnsglb1
dallpavnetlb001
 
This delegation zone works in round robin and hence when it hits grlnsglb1 since it doesn't have any information about the service present in Dallas it doesn't provide correct resolution.

• What is the impact to the business, how many policies were impacted?

All configured from PolicyCenter Account Contact / Additional Insured contact details are present in the generated certificate output.

Problem statement: EFT Payment Processing Impact – Life Claims
Description:
• Business Impact: Life Claims Users are unable to add bank account details for EFT claim payments due to a failure during single sign-on to a vendor application. As a result, claims requiring electronic payment setup are impacted, while paper check processing remains unaffected.
• RCA:  Cause Code: Undetermined, Cause Notes: After the 2023 cyber incident, AmFam's ADFS system was taken out of service, so we moved the One Inc SSO integration to Entra ID and it worked fine. During the recent MI, we found that One Inc's SSO started sending users back to the old ADFS login, which has been down for ~3 years, causing authentication failures/redirect loops. We asked One Inc to repoint their SSO back to Entra ID; once they did, we updated the Entra SAML EntityID to match the Issuer One Inc was sending, and One Inc cleared a caching issue on their side that was keeping the old redirect. After those changes, SSO started working normally again. Onc Inc need to verify why SSO configuration is pointed to AmFam owned Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS). when Raj (RVAIRAVA@amfam.com) asked One Inc during outage if there is anything changed on their side regarding to IDP configuration and One Inc said they didn't change anything on their side. As ADFS environment is not in operational state for last 3 years, fixing and move forward is the only way.
• Resolution:  Implement proposed fix once RCA has been completed. 
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No

Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2026044. Cause Code: software issue. Cause Notes: AFP13415 (BUILD COVERAGE SUMMARY REQUESTS – DAILY) and AFP13416 (BUILD COVERAGE SUMMARY REQUESTS – WEEKLY) are abending with NAT1302 (Division by zero not permitted). The program retrieves the Auto record count (ROW-COUNT) from the CSRT Billing DB2 table, and the JCL passes #PROCESS-ACTV-TYPE-SPLIT-LIMIT = '05'. If the Auto #ROW-COUNT is less than the PROCESS-ACTV-TYPE-SPLIT-LIMIT, the calculated group count truncates to zero (because PROCESS-ACTV-TYPE-GROUP-COUNT is defined as an integer), which leads to a subsequent divide-by-zero (NAT1302) abend. A subsequent calculation then attempts to divide CHK-SR-COUNT by PROCESS-ACTV-TYPE-GROUP-COUNT (0), causing the divide-by-zero abend. This issue is occurring because, after most policies were migrated, the remaining Auto policies in the CSRT table are now fewer than the configured PROCESS-ACTV-TYPE-SPLIT-LIMIT. As a result, both the daily and weekly jobs are impacted since they use the same AFP13415 program..

Problem statement: FRUConv - NE -RN - System:  PolicyCenter  Policy or Account Number(s): 910057879179 - application error when trying to quote
Description:
Description: Trying to quote and issue umbrella renewal. Error received. "an application error occurred. Stack Trace". When a Farm/Ranch Umbrella policy contains an underlying policy with 0/0/0 limits, the underlying policy removal logic executes correctly during the first policy term but is not invoked during renewal transactions (2nd term and beyond). The invalid underlying policy persists into the renewed term and causes a NullPointerException.

Root cause: 0/0/0-limit underlying policies are removed on Term 1 only; they persist on Term 2+ renewals that trigger/event path is not invoked, so the system never re-evaluates underlying limits and does not remove the 0-limit underlying policy and cause a fatal NPE during rating.  

Steps to Reproduce:
  1. Create and issue a FRU policy (Term 1) with at least one underlying policy carrying 0/0/0 limits (e.g., converted from ABEST
  with missing limit data).
  2. Allow or trigger a renewal to Term 2.
  3. Observe the 0/0/0-limit underlying policy is still present on the renewed term.
  4. Attempt to quote/rate the renewal.
  5. Result: Rating fails with NullPointerException in fru_iso_underlyingpolicy_rrv2.

Workaround:
Manually remove the underlying policy entry with 0/0/0 limits from the policy, then continue the transaction/renewal.

Problem statement: MyAccount Incorrect Policy Data
Description:
• Business Impact: Summary: MyAccount policy information is dispalying incorrect policy data within the MyAccount mobile applications. 
First Reported By: End User
Director Engaged: Brandon Wienkes | Michele Forgette 
Business Area(s) Impacted: MyAccount - Myamfam
Partner(s) Impacted: Costco
• RCA: Due to a recent change request from MyAccount application team, the delivery of the presigned URL was modified to present a more user-friendly document name. This was caused by incorrect implementation of this enhancement for the April 2026 Release. The change was made to documentpullv2 component to remove the identifier prefix from the filename generated for the presigned url document flow. Defect resulted in a nondistinct key being used across requests from different customers from the MyAccount application for downloads using presigned urls only. The reason a nondistinct key was injected into the response is due to the URL was created incorrectly by the documentpullv2 service. It was supposed to continue to use a key that had a distinct identifier but include an option that caused the download to use a different filename than the key in the S3 bucket. Instead of configuring that option, the distinct key was removed from both parts.
• Resolution: 1. Regression testing for Pre-signed URL concurrent access by MyAccount (added to our release testing process)
2. Include AC of testing signoff from the application team that requests a change to the feature (added to our JIRA process)
3. Code review Process - a) Updated weekly code review to daily code review to get the peer review completed quickly before that code is deployed to testing
b) Update JIRA workflow to ensure that development tasks cannot move to completed state (added manual verification process immediately, and we will work with JIRA team for automation in the future)
4. Analyzing the feasibility of Preventative Code Change to Enhance Document API V2 to specify the Presigned URL + version in URL for S3 Presigned URL - https://amfament.atlassian.net/browse/ECM-8728 to further mitigate any risks.
5. Analyzing S3 bucket monitoring options to see if we can detect a larger number of hits to a specific file

Description:
• Business Impact: Users are reporting an issue within the Horison Billing Screen displaying a timeout error. 
• RCA: Assigned to "AFI - Net Routers - Salman Raza "

Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025641. Cause Code: people process documentation. Cause Notes: DNS A records for four asgard.local hostnames were added to Enterprise-View in Infoblox instead of Partner-HOM, automatically creating a shadow authoritative asgard.local zone in Enterprise-View containing only those 4 records. The asgard.local zone is an Active Directory domain used by Homesite/Horison infrastructure, authoritative in the Partner-HOM view on the Enterprise Infoblox grid with 40+ host records. When Horison imainhs servers (imain11, imain12) queried Enterprise Infoblox for asgmarmsdmmq17.asgard.local (the MSMQ message queue server), the shadow zone responded authoritatively with NXDOMAIN — causing DRCSendRequest timeouts on the IBILL queue and cascading process crashes. The PDCC emptied their call queue and turned away all callers. Records incorrectly added to Enterprise-View: iso_db_prod.asgard.local → 10.206.220.21 (RITM3044642, manual GUI, no change request) web_db_prod.asgard.local → 10.206.220.22 (RITM3044642, manual GUI, no change request) SvcInfo_db_prod.asgard.local → 10.206.220.28 (RITM3044642, manual GUI, no change request) asgbosprdrts21.asgard.local → 192.168.196.45 (RITM3044513, CHG2190113 in "New" state, never approved) Contributing factors: Records created in wrong DNS view (Enterprise-View instead of Partner-HOM) No change request created or approved for RITM3044642/SCTASK2949300 CHG2190113 in "New" state — records implemented before change approval CI/CD pipeline bypassed — records created manually in the Infoblox GUI Pipeline failures not investigated before falling back to manual creation.
Close notes: Resolution Complete — INC5156687 Horison Billing Outage Root Cause: DNS A records for four asgard.local hostnames were added to Enterprise-View in Infoblox as part of ResultsCX requests (RITM3044513, RITM3044642). The asgard.local zone is an Active Directory domain authoritative only in the Partner-HOM view. Adding records to Enterprise-View automatically created a shadow authoritative zone containing only 4 records. When Horison imainhs application servers queried Enterprise Infoblox for asgmarmsdmmq17.asgard.local (MSMQ message queue server), the shadow zone returned NXDOMAIN, causing billing process connectivity failures, DRCSendRequest timeouts, and a complete PDCC call center shutdown. Contributing Factors: 1. Records were created manually in the Infoblox GUI, bypassing the CI/CD pipeline entirely 2. No change request was created for RITM3044642/SCTASK2949300 (the 3 db records that caused the P1) 3. CHG2190113 was still in "New" state when records were implemented — no approval obtained 4. CI/CD pipeline failures (3 attempts) were not investigated — manual GUI creation was used as a workaround 5. The requester specified "Enterprise-View" without understanding the zone architecture implications 6. Additional DNS record corruption occurred when the Partner-HOM host record for asgbosprdrts21.asgard.local was modified from the correct IP (10.20.1.124) to an incorrect IP (10.20.1.24) Resolution Actions: - Removed all 4 shadow zone A records from Enterprise-View (04/17/2026 14:15-14:28 CT) - Cleared DNS cache on msmq11 and ASGMARMSDMMQ17 - Full restart of imain11 application processes — confirmed back online at 14:51 CT - Corrected Partner-HOM host record for asgbosprdrts21.asgard.local back to 10.20.1.124 (documented in CHG2190141) Preventive Action Plan Implemented: 1. Enforce CI/CD pipeline for all Infoblox DNS changes — restrict GUI write access (In Progress) 2. Problem statement: Life Cornerstone Intermittent Log In Errors
Description:
• Business Impact: Life Cornerstone users are reporting that they are unable to log in because they are receiving a "Sign On Error: Single Sign On authentication unsuccessful (reference # Dxtxrdva)" error message.
• RCA: Assigned and Assess state
• Resolution: Implement proposed fix once RCA has been completed. 
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025633. Cause Code: Undetermined. Cause Notes: The Audit logs in Azure confirmed there were no configuration changes for Ipipeline instance in the last 30 days. All Azure Entra logs showed successful sign-ins during that time period. There were no configuration changes to the Conditional Access policies that interacts with user logins to the application in the last 30 days. There were no issues related to any of the 100s of other enterprise SSO apps configured for Azure. The SAML response from the user who could connect successfully after clearing their browser cache showed the Azure default token lifetime of being 1 hour. Amfam Azure tenant uses the default SAML token lifetime of 1 hour. There is no conditional access policy for the application configured to over-ride this setting. Based on some research it appears to be caused by some sort of time synch issue. Either on the app side that the app is not interpreting correctly what we are sending in the SAML response from Azure, possibly a time synch issue on the external application side or on the end users side. There was no SAML response captured for a user who could not connect, therefore we cannot determine if we were actually sending a token of over 75 minutes that the external app team was seeing in their logs. As this issue was intermittent in which not all users were affected, there might have been a time synch issue on the external.. From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025633. Cause Code: Undetermined. Cause Notes: No permanent fix as RCA is undeterminedPreventive Actions items:Confirm and document the current Azure SAML token lifetime setting for the AmFam tenant (default 1 hour) and verify there is no Conditional Access policy overriding token lifetime for this application. Establish a repeatable diagnostic playbook for iPipeline SSO issues (what logs to check: Azure Audit logs, Azure Entra sign-in logs, Conditional Access change history, and external app SSO logs). Proactively align with the external application team on time synchronization expectations (NTP/time drift tolerance) and logging requirements for SAML token validity/expiration interpretation. RCA WHEN IT OCCURS NEXT TIME:Capture a SAML trace from an affected user’s desktop/session while the issue is actively occurring (before clearing cache) to confirm the SAML assertion/token validity window being sent by Azure. Collect timestamps from all involved systems (end-user device time, browser time, Azure sign-in time, and external application log time) to validate/identify time drift or misinterpretation of token timestamps. Request the external app team provide the specific log evidence indicating a “75+ minute token” (or equivalent) and correlate it to the captured SAML assertion to confirm whether the issue is token lifetime, cache/session reuse, or time synchronization. Potential Risk (if any):Intermittent SSO access failures may recur for a subset of users, impacting business operations and increasing support volume. If time drift exists (end-user device or external application), authentication/session issues could expand beyond iPipeline and become more frequent or harder to troubleshoot without captured traces..
Close notes: Due to uncertainty to what caused this issue, there is no solution besides clearing the browser cache.

Problem statement: Production Job Failure - AFP13957 - Additional Check needed due to policy migration
Description:
We are encountering a job AFP13957 abend every day. This happens because the CSL file is empty. The CSL file is empty because there are no policies in the CSRT database, since most policies have been migrated to the new system.

This situation is expected, but the job still fails. To avoid this daily abend, we need to update the program AFP13956 to ignore the empty CSL file scenario and allow the process to complete normally.
Assignment group: Business Integrations and Support - Business Systems
Cause notes: We encountered an issue in production job AFP13957, Step080, where program AFP13956 returned code 0012. This was related to the empty CSL file. Since most policies have been migrated, policy volume is low, which is leading to this condition occurring in Production.. From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025523. Cause Code: software issue. Cause Notes: In Production, batch job AFP13957 failed in Step080 when program AFP13956 completed with return code 0012. The failure was triggered during processing of the CSL file, which was found to be empty for that run. Because most policies have been migrated to the new system, the remaining policy volume in the legacy source is now very low, and this “empty CSL” condition is occurring in Production more frequently. As a result, AFP13957 is experiencing an operational failure even though the underlying condition no CSL records due to low policy volume is expected in the post-migration state..
Close notes: The cause of the production failure is that program AFP13956 is designed to treat an empty CSL file as an error condition and responds by returning code 0012, which causes AFP13957 Step080 to fail. The CSL file is empty because the policy volume in the CSRT database has significantly decreased after the migration of most policies to the new system, leaving few or no eligible policies to generate CSL records. Therefore, the job is failing not due to a data defect, but due to existing error-handling logic in AFP13956 that does not account for the expected low volume of policies scenario in Production. To prevent this recurring daily abend and allow the batch cycle to complete successfully, the program AFP13956 code is being modified by commenting out the error-handling path so that an empty CSL results in a normal termination with return code 000 rather than error code 112, eliminating the daily abend condition.

Problem statement: Some Homesite Monitoring Unavailable
Description:
• Business Impact: Monitoring is unavailable for 50 affected Homesite servers, resulting in no visibility or alerts for those systems. Not all monitoring within Homesite is gone at the moment.  
• RCA: As part of PCI audit remediation, Team have been monitoring and migrating traffic off an overly permissive internet-exposed firewall rule (any/any) to a cloned, tightened rule for the past year. • Resolution: To validate, Team is adding a restricted outbound rule to the existing Datadog address group and disabling the open rule to confirm Datadog continues to function as expected. Going forward, team will proactively notify the Datadog team before removing permissive rules to avoid inadvertently blocking any required web-port traffic.

Approximately one year ago, we migrated all identified legitimate traffic off this open rule to a new cloned rule and have been maintaining/updating the cloned rule for the last three audits. After extensive review of the original open rule, I did not find any confirmed legitimate connections tied to it. Problem statement: EDW load issues
Description: EDW load issues
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025191. Cause Code: software issue. Cause Notes: Issue / Impact For policy BP00070264, three entity references alone generated 138,225,875 rows in WFL_ACTIVITY_HISTORY All these rows are tied to DocGen workflow retries with the error pattern: > “DOCUMENTS is failed for . The task is marked for sequential processing and is not yet completed in previous revision. After retrying for 1500 it is marked failed.” Because EDW delta loads use WFL_ACTIVITY_HISTORY as a driver table, this volume causes very large scans and severe EDW slowness / job failures. Technical Root Cause Sequential DocGen workflow configuration The affected workflow task is configured for sequential processing, i.e., it waits for document generation to complete on the previous revision before allowing the current revision to proceed. For these entities, that precondition was never satisfied, so the task kept re-evaluating the same “previous revision not complete” condition. Retry logic in Workflow processing The workflow engine identifies the next activity to process. When it finds a sequential DocGen task whose previous revision is not complete, it: does not move forward, logs a row in WFL_ACTIVITY_HISTORY with stage "Waiting for Document Generation to complete in previous revision", and increments an internal retry counter. The retry counter is currently set for 1500 attempts It means that the process described above repeats 1500 times and inserts 1500 records in the history table Such retries can happen multiple times within a day resulting in large volume of data in history table Repeated re-entry into the retry loop The same 3 DocGen activities for policy BP00070264 stayed in this stuck state from around 14-Jul-2025 to 9-Mar-2026 Batch/reprocessing logic repeatedly invoked the workflow engine for these activities. Each such invocation could re-run the 1500-attempt retry loop, adding another 1500 rows, until the task was marked failed for that run. Net Effect for EDW EDW delta logic depends on WFL_ACTIVITY_HISTORY timestamps (WAH_DATE_CREATED / WAH_DATE_MODIFIED) to identify changed records for many PAS tables (approx. 80% of PAS EDW extracts use this pattern). The huge volume of technical DocGen-retry rows for a few entities inflated the CDC set dramatically, causing: long-running queries and significant EDW batch delays, and in our case batch failure.
Close notes: Workaround: To execute EDW batch successfully, we have o blocked the transactions for this policy so that extraction process is not impacted o purged the 138M records for this entity from history table (This activity is completed today) o We will now unblock the transaction so that it is processed by EDW and flows into downstream systems (planned for tomorrow) o We will continue monitoring to proactively identify occurrence of such issue and prevent batch failure

Description:
• Business Impact: Multiple Servers of PLPC, CLPC and Enterprice Billing Center are unreachable impacting the ability to perform policy related activities.
• RCA: Cause Code: People/Process/Documentation, Cause Notes: The root cause was a manual change made via the Infoblox web GUI after an initial CICD pipeline deployment for new DNS IPs at the Minneapolis location; the manual step inadvertently applied a global override instead of a network-level change, leading to DNS suffix conflicts.
• Resolution: 
This is part of RCA - Proposed Fix preventive/permanent action item which will be tracked for resolution task separately.

1. Immediate — Expand CICD automation scope: Include DHCP property configuration (router gateways, DDNS domain overrides, domain suffix, DHCP member assignment) in the existing Claude + Git CICD pipeline for new site deployments, eliminating the need for manual GUI overrides - PTASK2025219

2. Short-term — Implement grid-level change alerting: Configure monitoring/alerting on Infoblox Grid DHCP property modifications to detect unintended grid-level changes in real-time via syslog or SNMP trap integration - PTASK2025220

3. Short-term — Restrict grid-level DHCP modification permissions: Evaluate Infoblox admin role-based access controls to limit Grid DHCP property modification to a restricted set of administrators, preventing standard operators from inadvertently modifying grid-level settings - PTASK2025221

4. Long-term — Engage Infoblox Support: Open a support case with Infoblox referencing NIOS 9.0.4-52074 and the audit log evidence to report the GUI object context issue. Request investigation into whether this is a known defect and whether a patch or UI enhancement is available that provides clearer visual differentiation between Grid-level and Network-level DHCP property editors. Furthermore engage them about security measures for GRID level changes. PTASK2025222

5. Long-term — Change validation: Implement a pre/post change validation script that captures Grid DHCP properties before and after new site deployments and flags any unintended grid-level modifications - PTASK2025223

Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025158. Cause Code: people process documentation. Cause Notes: During the execution of CHG2185784 for the new Minneapolis office site, DHCP network/scope creation was completed via CICD automation (Claude + Git pipeline). Following the automation, the operator performed manual DHCP property overrides (router gateways, DDNS domain, DHCP member assignment) via the Infoblox NIOS 9.0.4 GUI. While configuring network-level overrides within the 10.117.64.0/19 container view, the initial DHCP property modification was applied to the Grid DHCP object instead of the intended Network DHCP object, changing the global ddns_domainname and domain_name from corporate.amfam.com to amfam.com. A contributing factor is that the Infoblox NIOS GUI presents a nearly identical look and feel for DHCP property configuration at the Grid level versus the Network level. Both views display the same fields, layout, and override/inherit toggle controls, making it extraordinarily difficult to distinguish which object level is being modified, without very careful scrutiny. Additionally, Grid-level DHCP properties are configured by default to push inherited settings to all child objects (members, networks, ranges), meaning any unintended grid-level change immediately propagates enterprise-wide with no confirmation prompt or warning. There is no visual differentiation, breadcrumb indicator, or safeguard in the GUI that clearly alerts the operator when a modification targets the Grid DHCP object versus a Network DHCP object. The audit log confirms this was an isolated object context issue — the very first change, and all post-GRID subsequent identical override operations in the same workflow (7 networks, same fields, same workflow) correctly applied at the network level as Modified Network..

When 1 policy coverage code has 2 CC coverage types as mentioned above, if its a TNC policy, ECC considers only TNC version of the coverage for mapping by excluding the non TNC version of the same coverage. Problem statement: Multiple Application Sites Are Unreachable
Description:
• Business Impact: Multiple synthetic tests are failing with timeout errors indicating impact to applications including EDSP, B2B, OLS, Threatx, MyAmFam.com, MyAccount
• RCA: Cause Code: Vendor Issue, Cause Notes: During the incident window, traffic routed through the ThreatX platform for the amfam tenant experienced service disruption as sensor instances became unhealthy within the autoscaling group. As unhealthy instances were replaced, the issue persisted because newly spawned instances inherited the same configuration dependency. Backend origin systems remained operational and reachable throughout the incident. No data integrity issues or data loss occurred. 
• Resolution: ThreatX management agreed to notify Amfam with changes to their infrastructure. Amfam ThreatX support team will create Vendor changes in SNOW to document changes to Vendor's infrastructure. This will help us correlate changes on their infracture to future outages, lowering the time to resolution in future events. 
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025127. Cause Code: vendor issue. Cause Notes: ISE RCA INC5060182 - Major Incident | Multiple Application Sites Are Unreachable Incident Overview Incident Title: Major Incident | Multiple Application Sites Are Unreachable Incident ID / Ticket #: INC5060182 Date/Time of Incident: 03/03/2026 17:13:20 Reported By: Event Management Detected By: Datadog monitoring Impacted Systems/Services: All external facing web resources Severity Level: 1Critical Summary: During the incident window, traffic routed through the ThreatX platform for the amfam tenant experienced service disruption as sensor instances became unhealthy within the autoscaling group. As unhealthy instances were replaced, the issue persisted because newly spawned instances inherited the same configuration dependency. Backend origin systems remained operational and reachable throughout the incident. No data integrity issues or data loss occurred. Timeline of Events Time (Central Time) Event Description Action Taken By Whom 3/4/26 3:08 PM ThreatX begins partial decommission of IBM platform. ThreatX 3/4/26 5:03 PM ThreatX alerting regarding unhealthy sensors for Amfam begins to fire. ThreatX 3/4/26 5:39 PM Paul Lee reaches out to Eric Chicoine via teams Amfam 3/4/26 5:47 PM Amfam opens an urgent ticket regarding the outage asking for a resource to join their bridge. Amfam 3/4/26 5:52 PM ThreatX SOC joins the call. ThreatX 3/4/26 5:59 PM ThreatX SOC escalates directly to ENG leadership. ThreatX 3/4/26 6:41 PM ThreatX reverts change in IBM. ThreatX 3/4/26 6:43 PM Amfam confirms traffic is now flowing on their end. Amfam 3/4/26 7:10 PM All clear is given from the Amfam side Amfam Root Cause Analysis Immediate Cause: We initially investigated whether it was caused by an AWS outage, perhaps related to ongoing war in Iran. AWS had reported a drone attack on a Middle Eastern data center and indicated some impacts to their systems. ThreatX status page was showing all systems functional. Root Cause: The incident resulted from a legacy configuration dependency present in sensor version 3.20.0 that referenced infrastructure components from the previously utilized IBM platform. During the migration to AWS, the platform architecture was modernized; however, this configuration dependency remained present within the older sensor version. When the IBM environment began partial decommissioning on March 3rd, newly launched sensor instances running version 3.20.0 were unable to properly initialize due to the missing dependency. These initialization failures caused the sensors to fail their health checks within the autoscaling group. As the system attempted to replace unhealthy instances, the issue repeated with newly spawned sensor instances, resulting in a cascading degradation of sensor availability. Additionally, although monitoring alerts correctly detected the unhealthy sensor state, the alert response did not immediately initiate corrective action, allowing the degradation to progress. Unauthorized Changes: Vendor change. Contributing Factors: Sensor Version 4.0 would not have been impacted by this change. American Family was scheduled to fully upgrade to version 4.0 across all tenants by March 5th, 2026. This upgrade was cancelled/postponed until RCA was provided. RCA Cause: Legacy configuration dependency and premature decommissioning of IBM platform in ThreatX environment. Corrective Actions Taken The immediate mitigation was to revert the IBM platform decommissioning change, restoring the legacy dependency required for sensor version 3.20.0 initialization and health checks. The long-term resolution is to upgrade American Family Insurance to sensor version v4, which removes the legacy dependency entirely and prevents recurrence during future infrastructure management activities. Next Steps: ThreatX: • Maintain the IBM platform dependency required for some sensor configurations on version 3.20.0 until remaining tenants are upgraded. • Upgrade the American Family Insurance tenants to sensor version v4, eliminating the legacy IBM platform dependency. • Introduce automated validation checks to detect legacy infrastructure dependencies prior to infrastructure decommissioning events. • Implement dependency audits as part of platform migration and infrastructure retirement planning. • Improve monitoring response procedures to ensure rapid mitigation when sensor health degradation alerts are triggered. • Conduct internal corrective action and coaching with the analyst involved to reinforce expected alert response procedures. Amfam: No Amfam action required. Final Disposition ISE Responsible for Fix? ThreatX Another Team Responsible? APISEC team to reschedule Sensor upgrade to version 4.0 in near future. Disposition Notes: Discussions related to additional logging and reporting via Datadog. Lessons Learned & Recommendations How can we avoid this incident in the future? Discussions related to additional logging and reporting via Datadog. Additional Recommendations: Communication & Follow-Up Stakeholders Notified: Jonathan Hughes, Shaheen Abdul Jabbar, Matt Mais Date RCA Completed: 03/04/2026 Next Review/Follow-Up Date: 01/06/2026 Owner for Follow-Up: Eric Chicoine Author & Date Prepared by: Eric Chicoine Date: 03/04/2026.
Close notes: ThreatX management agreed to notify Amfam with changes to their infrastructure. Amfam ThreatX support team will create Vendor changes in SNOW to document changes to Vendor's infrastructure. This will help us correlate changes on their infracture to future outages, lowering the time to resolution in future events.

Description: Pureconnect is currently unable to access the S3 bucket preventing uploading of call/screen recordings as well as review of them.  TLS connections are failing with the following error:
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2025077. Cause Code: vendor issue. Cause Notes: Pureconnect lost connection on all environments due to a root certificate authority change implemented by Amazon AWS. Amazon changed their intermediary Starfield certificate for HTTPS requests to the G2 version of the Starfield certificate. This certificate change brought down communication and preventing recordings from being accessed or moved. No dataloss occurred as PureConnect stored the recordings on the Media Servers until connection could be restored. Root cause was from Amazon AWS changing their root authority certificate chain and PureConnect using its own independent application certificate store preventing any automatic certificate updates applied to the machine. This was previously handled by the vendor during upgrades and included with the upgrade packages, however as PureConnect is end of life, this has to be done manually..
Close notes: Pureconnect lost connection on all environments due to a root certificate authority change implemented by Amazon AWS. Amazon changed their intermediary Starfield certificate for HTTPS requests to the G2 version of the Starfield certificate. This certificate change brought down communication and preventing recordings from being accessed or moved. No dataloss occurred as PureConnect stored the recordings on the Media Servers until connection could be restored. Pureconnect does not use the Microsoft Certificate Store (certmgr.msc) and instead uses its own store located locally on the application drives. D:\I3\IC\Certificates\Media Retrieval\Client\Trusted We converted the public root authority certificates to the correct format for PureConnect using OpenSSL to generate the hash name. After adding in the new Amazon Root CA 1 and Starfield G2 certificates, communication with the S3 bucket was restored for all environments. Root cause was from Amazon AWS changing their root authority certificate chain and PureConnect using its own independent application certificate store preventing any automatic certificate updates applied to the machine. This was previously handled by the vendor during upgrades and included with the upgrade packages, however as PureConnect is end of life, this has to be done manually.

PLLS (EP22), CLL (DK20) and Life Letters (DL20) were getting PERMISSION DENIED when trying to write files or write to log files in SHARED_STORAGE directories. Setting write permissions to jbo101:Docserver /nfs/web/docserv within Emergency CHG2184874 restored service.

Vilas updates that we're still working on the core Root Cause of why the permissions were removed. We know that the owner wasn't present on the jbo101 shared directory. We're trying to find why this UID was showing on this AFI server. None of these groups have changed, so how this directory got PCI, which has nothing to do with PCI, but something on Wednesday ported over the user and group. We lost both the jbo101 as a user and doc server as a group. We're working with Jesse Grantman from Cyber Squad. It's something on the Unix side that seems to be changing the permissions to the directory and sub-directory. Cyber is confirming that nothing has changed on these accounts/groups, and they've been there for years. With the introduction of the PCI issue, we're wondering if there was something that happened on Wednesday on the PCI side that propagated to non-PCI systems.

From the storage side, they don't modify any of the permissions. On the Linux side, they mount the shares but also don't modify the related permissions. Storage indicated that security manages the permissions on those shares. The share that we're talking about is nfs/web. This was originally setup to be managed under jbo101:Docserver. We know that the Linux team hasn't made any changes to the ownership structure here. We verified no application requests came in to touch this. The system logs didn't contain any commands that were run to change ownership. Our resolution during the incident was to change ownership to jbo101:Docserver, and then apply that to all of the files/folders recursively. As we were unable to fix it with a Unix permissions change, that's not something that ICS can normally do. ICS would normally give the service account or the group permission to do something.

This share is shared between six (three active/three passive) production nodes. In theory any of these six nodes could have been responsible for changing these permissions. We've checked the available logs on these six nodes and nothing appears to have been done on/by these nodes. It's also a Samba share. /nfs/web is the mount path, and docserv is the folder at which the permissions were updated to fix the issue. The fact that the jbo101 ID has been modified to another UID and GID would make us think it's another server that was doing some modifications here. We may need to focus the investigation on the PCI side, as you cannot on an LX/UX change the ownership to a non-existent group or user. But if I'm on a separate server where that group does exist, it would let me change the ownership to something that the other servers might not recognize. We checked this on the PCI nodes but also didn't see anything indicating a command being run (whether by a process or a user.)

If it's mounted at web, than anything connected at NFS could change the permissions on /docserv. The PCI environment was recently built and cutover in September 2025. As a theory, the application team may have requested access to this path to read files, but we're unable to find any record of such request. Is it possible to setup some sort of monitoring/alerting for this share that will report on any changes to this share? Vilas indicates it's not impossible, but we'll have to draft a plan and have a meeting with the DataDog team to see what may be possible.

Description:
Description: FRU/FO: Unable to bind transactions due to Licensing error, even when the agent has authorization rights to sell in that state.

Root Cause: 
When users are trying to bind the transaction, in the AuthorizedToSellRequest we are passing the attribute companyCode as null, which is being responded back as a Bad request with 400 error code from PMACS.

Earlier we're querying partner with PartnerID_AFI = null in fetchUWComapnies_AFI(), which was changed after release 60.0.0 making the value null in the request.

Proposed Fix:
Need to fix the logic in fetchUWComapnies_AFI() method in AvailableUWCompanies.gs file. 

Workaround: Can disable the 'EnableLicenseCheck' script parameter, after validating the request and response using the postman.

Problem statement: Progressive Partner Policy Document Printing Issue
Description:
Business Impact:
Between December 11, 2025, and January 25, 2026, 330,000 policy documents for Progressive partner customers were not printed or mailed due to a processing failure.

Issue Identification:
On January 26, 2026, the Correspondence Pipeline (Quadient) team detected an abnormal backlog of documents. Investigation against SmartCOMM reconciliation database revealed that Progressive partner documents were not processed between December 11, 2025 and January 25, 2026.

Root Cause (Preliminary):
Documents were generated and stored as expected, but the Progressive partner folder was unavailable for processing by Quadient during the affected period. The folder's unavailability is unusual and the exact cause is still under investigation.

Troubleshooting & Support:
1. VMWare Support: No performance issues detected.
2. AWS Support : A file gateway reboot occurred on January 25, 2026, possibly related to a software patch. AWS is investigating if this impacted folder visibility. The ticket is escalated to FileGateway servicing team with all S3 access logs shared for the working folder along with the Progressive folder and also enabling bidirectional access to the VMware.
3. Quadient Support: Consulting for similar incidents and expertise .


Recovery:
System recovered automatically after the AWS file gateway reboot that occurred on January 25,2026 at 1:25 AM CST and Quadient logs confirming the first progressive file started process on January 25,26 at 3:00 AM CST.

For the impacted customers there are several remediation steps taken based on guidance from the business and complaince team that are documented in  
https://amfament.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/E1PAP1CC/pages/17468391609/Progressive+ReProcess+Tracking


Remediation & Next Steps:
While RCA is yet to be confirmed team acknowledges better checkout process could have notified teams earlier that could have limited the exposure.

Immediate improvements underway:
1.Enhanced alerting with Homesite Reconciliation Process.
2. Notification for zero print files with major partners.
3. Alerts for unprocessed print files beyond a 24-hour threshold.
4. Migration to architecture eliminating FileGateway dependency.

A broader Enterprise Reconciliation Process is being designed for long-term prevention.
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2024911. Cause Code: Undetermined. Cause Notes: Detailed Flow diagram Homesite Business Flow - E1P Applications - Content Creation & Forms - Confluence The suspicion is with the AWS File Gateway which is used to share files between AWS and on-prem server. As the available logs did not list any anomalies, we involved AWS filegateway service for assistance, AWS case# 177039894500600. Based on the logs AWS pointed out there could be a racing condition between the high-volume file operations we perform against their indexing process. AWS support had us walk thru our process and tried recreating the flow in their environment so we can conclude the analysis, But they weren't able to. Though we are implementing changes that are outlined in the proposed fix notes that would alert the on call when the files are not processed within the business SLA..

Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2024804. Cause Code: vendor issue. Cause Notes: Salesforce pushed a change to require SF MFA for users logging in using SSO when certain criteria have not been met. Despite having our IP addresses whitelisted it was still requiring users to go through the SF MFA process. Working with SF support as part of SF Case 472641652 to further analyze what is causing the request for SF MFA for our ODIC SSO users. Changes to Device Activation for Single Sign-On (SSO) Logins.. From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2024804. Cause Code: vendor issue. Cause Notes: Salesforce pushed a change to require SF MFA for users logging in using SSO when certain criteria have not been met. Despite having our IP addresses whitelisted it was still requiring users to go through the SF MFA process. Working with SF support as part of SF Case 472641652 to further analyze what is causing the request for SF MFA for our ODIC SSO users. Changes to Device Activation for Single Sign-On (SSO) Logins SThe recent change that Salesforce implemented is meant to increase platform security by ensuring that the SSO methods being used by users are a strong authorization method. If the SSO authorization method is not considered strong OR if it is missing, then Salesforce is directing the users to set up MFA. This has to be done at an individual user level. The chart below shows the matrix for when users are prompted to activate devices using MFA. In looking at our logins within Salesforce platform, Sean noticed that we currently do not have an AMR (authorization method reference) recorded for our SSOs. Since we are not sending the AMR in the identity token back to SF when authenticating the users via Azure SSO, it is forcing users to go through device activation. If we can have Azure send the AMR as part of the identity token when a user logins in via SSO, this should resolve the issue and not force users to be prompted to activate their device..
Close notes: Entra endpoint moved to v1 to have AMR sent with identity token. MFA exemption for Mobile relate users removed 3/17. Description:
Description: CLPC: FR: Exception during retrieval of forms from FDM. Might be applicable to all LOBs.

Rootcause: The system is trying to retrieve the forms based on the written date of the transaction instead of effective date of the transaction. Scenario: Occurred during the creation of a back dated transaction for example creating a 2025 term transaction in 2026, which contains a form that is expired on 31st December 2025. As per CLPC logic it would be inferred, but in FDM it will not be retrieved as we are passing today's date. So, the mismatch occurs. 

Proposed Fix: Need to fix the inference logic of forms from FDM. 
File Name: FormsAPIHelper.gs
Function: getProductForms()

Workaround: Update expiration date of this form in Production OR update the FDM for until we reinfer the forms and revert it back later.

Problem statement: Classic Mainframe Autoplus policies unable to update
Description:
• Business Impact: Users unable to make changes to classic auto policies within Autoplus.
• RCA:  Cause Code: People, Process, Documentation. 
                  Cause Notes: 
-> Due to the abrupt delay in the nightly batch one of the crucial job - AF100017, which is responsible for re-                      enabling the AUTOPLUS (OPT 74), was not ran due to negative CA7 scheduler dependency with the JOB - AF100016 and AFP42001.
-> ROME migration / MPV batch job started failing. JOB AFP42001 started failing on January 20th, 2026 (Tuesday) at 23:18 PM CST, due to webservice PolicySummaryServiceV6 issue. AUTOPLUS Support team would not able to find the correct group of people in AT-PRODUCT-SERVICES at that time, and decided to start excluding impacted policies – it leaded to 15 manual restart and exclusion of the policies before the JOB AFP42001 ultimately completed on January 21th, 2026 (Wednesday) at 09:52 AM CST. Due to the same mainframe nightly batch was delayed by 8 hours.
-> Looks like notification protocol is not followed by AT-PRODUCT-SERVICES team for the webservice – PolicySummaryServiceV6 schema changes implementation. All of the webservice consumers should receive the change notification and test the changes along with CICS admin team (As this service is still getting consumed by mainframe applications via CICS).
• Resolution:   
- AUTOPLUS team worked with Operation (Ops) team to post the requirement for AF100016 à AF100017 to execute, and JOB completed re-enabled AUTOPLUS (OPT 74) and allow user to login / enter into the Application. 
- To bring back the application to update mode , application team manually execute AFP15105 and AFP15107 via Runsheet and application up to edit mode. 
- Created More Ptasks for permanent fix and to avoid the similar issue in future.

Problem statement: Permissions issue with users in Fusion Policy Center
Description:
• Business Impact: Currently users are unable to access Fusion
• RCA: The 'CustomList ADL Files BatchProcess' batch job is executed after every deployment to load updated ADL into production, whereas the system expects roles to be loaded first, followed by their associated roleprivileges. But the sequence was wrong we had roleprivileges first and then the roles for this release.  In this release 59.1.0, a new role and a new permission were introduced. Since the parent role did not exist at the time permissions were loaded, the permission load failed. This failure caused the permission load process to terminate, resulting in no permissions being loaded into production.
Impact:
           All permissions were missing in production after batch completed.
           User access was impacted until remediation steps were taken.
• Resolution: Mitigation & Preventive Actions:
Improve Permission Load Resiliency
We would plan to update the permission-loading logic to make it more fault-tolerant. If a single permission fails to load due to missing or invalid dependencies, the process will:

Skip the failed permission
Continue loading all remaining valid permissions
This prevents a single configuration issue from causing a complete permission load failure.
Align Deployment Validation with Production
To prevent recurrence, we plan to replicate the production load sequence and dependency conditions in QA.

This will ensure:
Role-permission dependency issues are detected earlier
Production-specific sequencing problems are validated before release
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: Yes/CHG2180758
